faq.q: What is the origin of Alassane?
faq.a: Alassane is associated with Arabic. Alassane is the West African form of Arabic الْحَسَن (al-Ḥasan), meaning 'good, handsome'.
Yes — the underlying form الْحَسَن is Arabic.
Alassane can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Alassane should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ح س ن is Quranic, but al-Ḥasan is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Alassane mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Alassane is rendered حسن and carries the sense حسن، نیکو.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-las-sa-ne. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Alassane, alassane. Script forms are الحسن, الْحَسَن, حسن, अलासाने.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
